test_split_note: No public construction path to RationalBezierSpan2 exists (constructor is pub(crate); CurveSpan2 exposes only from_line/from_circular_arc), so per the packet the curve-form conformance (hull_curve_homogeneous, incl. required test #8 and the curve-form parts of #4/#7) lives in the #[cfg(test)] mod tests inside src/hull.rs (same-crate access to ::new, the crate's existing pattern). tests/hull_conformance.rs covers the pub kernels, the derivative transforms, HullRefusal, and the source scan.

design_notes.de_casteljau_node_arrangement: The kernel keeps the packet's mandated discipline (de Casteljau over the OUTWARD-ROUNDED CertifiedInterval subinterval parameter, every coefficient widened through CertifiedInterval::point). The node step is arranged as the subdivision form pts[i] + u*(pts[i+1]-pts[i]) instead of (1-u)*pts[i] + u*pts[i+1]: algebraically identical for scalar u, sound at every degree (interval arithmetic is inclusion-monotone), and it makes the degree-1 hull exactly the endpoint range. The packet's required test linear_span_hull_is_the_exact_range is impossible under the dependency-widened convex-combination arrangement (a linear hull over (0.2,0.8) evaluates to [0.6,2.4] instead of the exact [0.78,2.22]); the subdivision arrangement resolves that internal tension while staying within 'de Casteljau evaluation with the subinterval as a CertifiedInterval parameter'.
design_notes.non_finite_hull_example: Test non_finite_hull_refuses_enclosure_unavailable uses [f64::MAX, -f64::MAX] over a strict-interior subinterval rather than the packet's illustrative '[f64::MAX, f64::MAX]': under the subdivision arrangement the constant polynomial [MAX, MAX] evaluates exactly to [MAX, MAX] (finite, no sum overflow), whereas the difference -MAX - MAX overflows the CertifiedInterval subtraction, so the strict-interior hull refuses EnclosureUnavailable. Same named case, same mechanism class (finite coefficients, overflowing de Casteljau intermediate); documented in the test comment.
design_notes.reversed_domain: hull_curve_homogeneous maps sub through the span's OWN source-to-unit affine map (RationalBezierSpan2::domain_to_unit semantics), not the sorted-domain map, because the reversed span's coefficients are its own and must NOT be reversed (per packet). The compactness check uses the sorted (canonical) domain. Verified by the in-module reversed-domain test.
design_notes.division_used_only_for_parameter_map: unit_subinterval evaluates the source-to-unit affine map in CertifiedInterval arithmetic using CertifiedInterval::div (the packet's 'computed in CertifiedInterval arithmetic (widened)'); no dehomogenization happens anywhere in the module - X/Y/W are returned homogeneous. The module's own code contains no '/' operator at all (asserted by the source scan); the in-module tests divide only f64 values.
design_notes.no_unwrap_expect_panic: hull.rs carries no unwrap/expect/panic and no module-level allow (H-1); the in-module tests use match/ok patterns instead. Crate-level #![deny(clippy::unwrap_used)] enforced by compilation.
